title: Nuevo Laredo Touts 7.4 Billion Pesos in Public Works at National Infrastructure Congress
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's mayor told a national infrastructure congress that the city has put 7.445 billion pesos into more than 1,600 public works — the most...
content:
Nuevo Laredo's mayor told a national infrastructure congress that the city has put 7.445 billion pesos into more than 1,600 public works — the most of any municipality in Tamaulipas, according to the city government — and pointed to water, drainage and highway projects as the backbone of that investment.

Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal took part in the Congreso Nacional de Infraestructura 2026, led by Tamaulipas Governor Américo Villarreal Anaya and organized by the state Public Works Secretariat and the Mexican Chamber of the Construction Industry. The gathering brought together authorities, specialists, business owners and construction industry representatives to plan strategic projects for the state and the country.

Among the projects the mayor highlighted is more than 2.5 billion pesos in hydraulic infrastructure, covering more than 60 kilometers of collectors, subcollectors and sanitary and storm drainage networks. According to the city, those works have strengthened the city's response to rainfall, preventing street and neighborhood flooding during recent rains, and have contributed to cleaning up the Rio Bravo — an issue that matters on both sides of the border.

On connectivity, the municipal government put more than 283 million pesos of its own funds toward the MEX-2 highway, one of the main routes to the World Trade Bridge, resolving a backlog of more than 25 years. The city also pointed to its Museum of Science, Technology and Planetarium, a space of more than 4,000 square meters built with 280 million pesos in a converted former water tank, as part of its push into education, culture and science.

The Canturosas administration also says it has paid off 580 million pesos in inherited bank debt while carrying out the works, which the city presents as proof that the investment has not come at the cost of the municipality's finances.

Sources: Sin Censura, Nov. 27, 2026; Gobierno Municipal de Nuevo Laredo.
